blind_spots_patched: Baseline chapters only mentioned 'at least one client above 10%' without quantifying the 25.0% single-customer revenue share, 46.5% top-5 customer share, 50% top-10 receivables concentration, and 91.3% external IC substrate dependence.

Baseline ch-6 stopped at Dec 31, 2025 debt, missing the +53.9% debt surge to NT$406,461M by Sep 30, 2026, -NT$115,929M 9M 2026 FCF, 2027 debt maturity wall (US$2.5B USD variable loans + NT$47.4B NT$ loans), NT$135.2B PP&E purchase commitments, and Note 37(e) customer advance deposits.

Baseline chapters treated export controls as purely beneficial without analyzing the Nov 18, 2026 U.S. BIS AI export rule tightening, ASE's 75.4% Taiwan / 13.8% China asset mismatch vs. 56.7% U.S. billing, USD/NTD FX swap distortion, and Taiwan power/PPA cost inflation.

Baseline ch-4 omitted Intel Foundry's interposer-free EMIB-T entering AI ASIC packaging (MediaTek/Google), TSMC's planned CoWoS doubling to 260k–290k wpm by 2028 + CoPoS, and Amkor's $12B CHIPS/ITC-subsidized Arizona expansion.
assumptions_changed: BROKEN: Inside EMS (USI), management rotated away from consumer communications into Automotive (41% of Q3 2026 EMS revenue) and Industrial (21%), while FY2025 geographic revenue was Taiwan 12.1%, Asia excl. Taiwan 17.6%, Europe 12.0%, and Others 1.6%.
CONFIRMED: LEAP and ATM momentum are driving Q4 2026 sequential expansion (guided +6%–8% QoQ consolidated revenue and +11%–13% QoQ ATM revenue) while EMS cools sequentially.
WEAKENED: ASE carries manageable balance-sheet leverage (NT$264,097M total debt, NT$171,628M net debt, NT$1,712M net interest expense covered ~30x as of Dec 31, 2025) while funding AI CapEx.
WEAKENED: ASE and Amkor (~$2B Arizona campus) enjoy a protected Western AI OSAT duopoly shielded by TSMC's chronic CoWoS bottleneck.
CONFIRMED: ASE's consignment wafer model avoids die inventory risk and insider governance/share count remain stable.
